examples.en: Our body maintains homeostasis of body temperature.

examples.ko: 땀을 흘리는 것도 몸의 항상성에 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Sweating also helps the body's homeostasis.
We learned what homeostasis is in class.
The body's homeostasis is sometimes regulated by hormones.
A question on homeostasis came up in the biology exam.
I learned about the importance of homeostasis from a video.

explain: 생물 수업이나 건강 기사에서 주로 나오는 말이에요. '체온 항상성', '항상성을 유지하다'처럼 '유지하다'와 자주 함께 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '몸이 균형을 맞추다'처럼 쉽게 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: This word mostly appears in biology classes and health articles. It often pairs with '유지하다' (to maintain), as in '체온 항상성' or '항상성을 유지하다'. In daily talk people say things like '몸이 균형을 맞추다' (the body keeps its balance).

examples.en: The people of that city resisted to the very end.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 항전 의지를 밝혔다는 소식이 나왔어요.
examples.en: The news reported that they declared their will to resist.

examples.ko: 군인들은 며칠 동안 항전을 이어 갔어요.
examples.en: The soldiers kept up their resistance for several days.

examples.ko: 영화에서 마지막 항전 장면이 인상 깊었어요.
examples.en: The final scene of resistance in the movie was impressive.
We learned about the course of the resistance in history class.
It is not easy to keep fighting with a small force.

explain: 그냥 '싸우다'보다 훨씬 무겁고, 강한 상대에 맞서 끝까지 버티며 싸운다는 느낌이 있어요. '항전 의지', '항전을 벌이다'처럼 뉴스나 역사 글에서 주로 보여요.
explain_en: It is much heavier than a plain '싸우다' (to fight) and carries the feeling of standing up to a stronger opponent and holding out to the end. You mostly see it in news and history texts, as in '항전 의지' (will to resist).

en: appeasing one's thirst; quenching one's thirst

examples.ko: 오랜 가뭄 끝에 내린 비로 해갈이 됐어요.
examples.en: The rain after a long drought relieved the dryness.

examples.ko: 농부들은 비가 와서 해갈을 기대하고 있어요.
examples.en: The farmers are hoping the rain will relieve the drought.

examples.ko: 등산 중에 마신 얼음물이 최고의 해갈이었어요.
examples.en: The ice water I drank while hiking was the perfect thirst quencher.

examples.ko: 물 한 잔으로는 해갈은 어림도 없어요.
examples.en: One glass of water is nowhere near enough to quench my thirst.

examples.ko: 해갈 효과가 좋아서 여름에 이 음료를 자주 마셔요.
examples.en: It quenches thirst well, so I often drink this beverage in summer.

examples.ko: 이번 비는 해갈에 큰 도움이 될 거예요.
examples.en: This rain will be a big help in relieving the drought.

explain: 목마름을 푸는 것뿐 아니라, 가뭄 끝에 비가 와서 메마른 땅이 풀리는 것에도 써요. 그래서 뉴스에서는 '가뭄 해갈'이라는 말을 자주 들어요. 일상에서 목마름은 '갈증이 풀리다', '목을 축이다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Besides quenching thirst, it is used when rain relieves a drought, so you often hear '가뭄 해갈' in the news. In everyday talk, people say '갈증이 풀리다' or '목을 축이다' for thirst.

en: appease one's thirst; quench one's thirst

examples.en: I quenched my thirst with a glass of cool water.
I quenched my thirst with stream water on the mountain and climbed again.

examples.ko: 이 음료는 마시면 금방 해갈해 줘요.
examples.en: This drink quenches your thirst quickly.

examples.ko: 더운 날에는 수박으로 해갈하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: On hot days, many people quench their thirst with watermelon.

examples.ko: 물 한 잔으로는 해갈할 수 없어요.
examples.en: One glass of water cannot quench my thirst.

examples.ko: 목마른 아이가 해갈하려고 물을 벌컥벌컥 마셨어요.
examples.en: The thirsty child gulped down water to quench his thirst.

explain: '갈증을 풀다', '목을 축이다'보다 글 같은 말이라 일상 대화에서는 덜 써요. 글이나 광고, 설명문에서 볼 수 있어요. '갈증'과 뜻이 겹치므로 '갈증을 해갈하다'보다 '해갈하다'만 쓰는 편이 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is more written-style than '갈증을 풀다' or '목을 축이다', so it is used less in daily talk. You may see it in writing, ads and explanatory texts. Since its meaning already includes thirst, plain '해갈하다' sounds more natural than '갈증을 해갈하다'.

examples.en: I soak the clams in salt water to remove the sand.

examples.ko: 바지락은 요리하기 전에 꼭 해감해야 해요.
examples.en: You must purge the sand from the clams before cooking.
I purged the clams of sand last evening.

examples.ko: 해감하는 동안 조개를 어두운 곳에 두세요.
examples.en: Keep the clams in a dark place while they purge.
If you don't purge them, you will bite into sand in the soup.
Mom is purging the clams of sand.

explain: 주로 조개처럼 모래나 개흙을 머금은 해산물에 쓰는 요리 말이에요. 요리 레시피에서 '조개 해감하기'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a cooking word used mainly for shellfish like clams that hold sand or mud. You often see it in recipes, as in '조개 해감하기'.

examples.en: I took a walk in the neighborhood park at dusk.
When dusk came, the sky turned red.
I was on my way home around dusk.

examples.ko: 시골에서는 해거름이면 저녁 짓는 냄새가 났어요.
examples.en: In the countryside, the smell of dinner cooking drifted by at dusk.
The beach at dusk was truly beautiful.
We worked in the field until dusk.

explain: 해가 지기 시작하는 무렵을 말하는데, '저녁'보다 글 같고 정서적인 느낌이 있어요. 같은 때를 '해 질 녘'이라고도 해요. 소설이나 시골 풍경을 이야기할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It refers to the time when the sun begins to set, and feels more literary and sentimental than '저녁' (evening). The same time is also called '해 질 녘'. It suits novels and descriptions of countryside scenery.

examples.en: I had a bizarre dream this morning.
That person's behavior is so bizarre.

examples.ko: 어른들이 보시기에 그 옷차림은 해괴했나 봐요.
examples.en: That outfit must have looked outlandish to the elders.
A strange-looking fish was caught in the net.
Everyone says that rule is absurdly strange.
It was so bizarre that I couldn't even laugh.

explain: '이상하다'보다 훨씬 센 말이에요. 어이없고 못마땅한 느낌이 들어서 소문, 일, 옷차림 같은 것에 써요. 사람에게 직접 쓰면 무례하게 들릴 수 있어요. 일상에서는 '이상하다', '황당하다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is much stronger than '이상하다' (strange), with a feeling of disbelief and disapproval, used for rumors, events or outfits. Said directly about a person it can sound rude. In daily speech people use '이상하다' or '황당하다' more often.

examples.en: We went to the west coast to watch the sunset.
A sunset event is held on December 31st.
This place is famous for its beautiful sunsets.
We arrived at the beach just in time for the sunset.

examples.ko: 해넘이와 해돋이를 둘 다 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to see both the sunset and the sunrise.
They say today's sunset is around five thirty.

explain: 해가 지는 일이나 그 순간을 가리키는 순우리말이고, 짝말은 '해돋이'예요. 한자어 '일몰'과 같은 뜻인데 더 부드럽게 들려요. 연말에는 '해넘이 행사'라는 말을 자주 들어요.
explain_en: This native Korean word refers to the sun setting, and its counterpart is '해돋이' (sunrise). It means the same as the Sino-Korean '일몰' but sounds softer. At year's end you often hear '해넘이 행사'.

en: relevant field; relevant space; relevant box

examples.en: Please write your name in the relevant box.
I filled in all the relevant fields of the application.

examples.ko: 해당란이 비어 있으면 접수가 안 돼요.
examples.en: If the relevant field is empty, it can't be accepted.

examples.ko: 해당되는 항목이 없으면 해당란은 비워 두세요.
examples.en: If no item applies, leave that field blank.
Please sign below the relevant box.

examples.ko: 해당란과 다른 내용을 쓰면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not write anything different from what that field asks.

explain: 서류나 설문 양식에서 '해당하는 칸'을 가리킬 때 써요. '해당란에 표시하세요', '해당란에 기입'처럼 안내문에 자주 나와요. 말로 할 때는 그냥 '그 칸'이라고 해도 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It points to the matching box on a form or survey. It often appears in instructions like '해당란에 표시하세요' (mark the relevant box). In speech, simply saying '그 칸' (that box) also sounds natural.

examples.ko: 뱀에 물리면 빨리 해독제를 맞아야 해요.
examples.en: If a snake bites you, you must get the antidote quickly.
This hospital has the antidote ready.
The antidote differs depending on the type of poison.

examples.ko: 이 약은 중독 사고에 해독제로 쓰여요.
examples.en: This medicine is used as an antidote in poisoning accidents.
It's even scarier because it's a poison with no antidote.
Developing the antidote took several years.

explain: 독을 풀어 주는 약이에요. 의학 뉴스나 영화에 자주 나오고, 비유로도 많이 써요. 몸속 독을 뺀다는 '해독'과 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: Laughter is the antidote to stress.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 것을 없애 주는 좋은 것을 비유할 때 써요. 글이나 연설에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for something good that counteracts something bad. Common in writing and speeches.

explain_en: This is a medicine that neutralizes poison. It appears often in medical news and movies, and is also commonly used figuratively. It is good to learn it together with '해독' (detoxification).

examples.en: I looked up the dream interpretation, and it says it's a good dream.

examples.ko: 할머니의 해몽대로 정말 좋은 일이 생겼어요.
examples.en: Just as Grandma interpreted, something really good happened.
According to dream interpretation, a pig dream brings good fortune.
That dream interpretation is take it or leave it.

examples.ko: 해몽이 좋아서 하루 종일 기분이 좋았어요.
examples.en: The interpretation was good, so I felt great all day.
There are many dream interpretation sites on the internet.

explain: 꿈이 무엇을 뜻하는지 풀이하는 것을 말해요. 보통 '꿈 해몽'이라고 붙여서 많이 말해요. '좋은 해몽', '나쁜 해몽'처럼 풀이 결과를 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 별것 아닌 일을 그렇게 좋게 보다니, 꿈보다 해몽이 좋네요.
phrases.en: You see such good in something so ordinary. The interpretation is better than the dream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 별것 아닌 일을 그럴듯하게 좋게 풀이할 때 써요. 재치 있게 또는 살짝 비꼬듯이 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when someone puts a good spin on something ordinary. It sounds witty or slightly teasing.
phrases.en_equiv: to put a positive spin on it

explain_en: This is the act of explaining what a dream means. People often say it together as '꿈 해몽'. You can also use it for the result, as in '좋은 해몽' (a good interpretation).

en: read a dream; interpret a dream

examples.en: A fortune-teller interpreted my dream for me.

examples.ko: 꿈을 어떻게 해몽하느냐에 따라 기분이 달라져요.
examples.en: Your mood changes depending on how you interpret a dream.
Grandma interpreted the dream in a good way.

examples.ko: 이 책은 꿈을 해몽하는 방법을 알려 줘요.
examples.en: This book teaches how to interpret dreams.

examples.ko: 돼지꿈을 꿨다고 하니까 친구가 복권 꿈이라고 해몽했어요.
examples.en: When I said I dreamed of a pig, my friend read it as a lottery dream.
As I read the dream, that's a good sign.

explain: 꿈을 풀이할 때 쓰는 말이에요. '꿈을 좋게 해몽하다'처럼 어떻게 풀이하는지 말하는 표현과 잘 어울려요. 일상에서는 '꿈풀이를 하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is used when interpreting a dream, and works well with phrases about how you read it, like '꿈을 좋게 해몽하다'. In daily talk people also say '꿈풀이를 하다'.

examples.ko: 해묵은 감정을 이제는 털어 버리고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to shake off these long-standing feelings now.
This soybean paste is aged, so it has a deep flavor.
The conflict between the two is already long-standing.
I have to finish this long-overdue homework, even now.
When a problem gets old, it becomes harder to solve.
Some things become more valuable the older they get.

explain: 대부분 '해묵은 문제', '해묵은 감정'처럼 '해묵은' 형태로 명사 앞에 써요. '오래된'과 비슷하지만 문제, 감정, 빚처럼 오래 쌓여 온 것에 잘 어울려요. 간장이나 장처럼 오래 두는 음식에도 써요.
explain_en: It is mostly used in the form '해묵은' before a noun, as in '해묵은 문제'. It is similar to '오래된' (old) but fits things that have piled up for a long time, such as problems, feelings and debts. It also works for foods left to age, like soy sauce.

examples.en: When the exam ended, I felt a huge sense of freedom.
A sense of liberation washed over me the moment I left work.

examples.ko: 회사를 그만둔 뒤의 해방감은 말로 다 못 해요.
examples.en: I can't put into words the freedom I felt after quitting my job.
Drunk on the feeling of freedom, I played with friends all night.

examples.ko: 긴 장마가 끝나니 해방감 같은 게 느껴져요.
examples.en: Now that the long rainy season is over, I feel something like liberation.
A sense of freedom and anxiety came at the same time.

explain: 부담이나 구속에서 벗어났을 때의 시원한 기분이에요. '해방감을 느끼다', '해방감을 맛보다', '해방감을 만끽하다'처럼 써요. '자유로움'보다 힘든 일이 끝난 직후의 느낌에 더 잘 맞아요.
explain_en: It is the refreshing feeling of getting free from a burden or restraint, used as '해방감을 느끼다', '해방감을 맛보다' or '해방감을 만끽하다'. Compared with '자유로움', it fits the feeling right after something hard ends.

examples.en: During the thaw, roads weaken, so you need to be careful.
Spring has come and the thaw has begun.

examples.ko: 남북 관계가 해빙기를 맞았다는 뉴스가 나왔어요.
examples.en: The news said relations between the two Koreas have entered a thaw.

examples.ko: 해빙기 낙석 사고를 조심하라는 안내 문자가 왔어요.
examples.en: I got a text message warning about rockfall accidents during the thaw.

examples.ko: 해빙기의 산길은 비가 오면 더 미끄러워요.
examples.en: Mountain paths in the thaw season are even slipperier in the rain.
The thaw between the two countries didn't last long.

explain: 얼음과 눈이 녹는 시기를 말해요. 그래서 안전 안내에서 '해빙기 안전 점검'이라는 말이 나와요. 사이가 나빴던 나라나 사람들 관계가 풀리는 때에도 비유로 써요.

phrases.example: 두 나라 관계가 오랜만에 해빙기를 맞았어요.
phrases.en: Relations between the two countries have finally entered a thaw.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼음이 녹는다는 뜻에서 나아가, 오래 굳어 있던 사이가 풀리기 시작할 때 써요. 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Beyond melting ice, it describes when a long-frozen relationship begins to ease. Common in news.

explain_en: It refers to the time when ice and snow melt, so you see it in safety notices like '해빙기 안전 점검'. It is also used figuratively for when relations between countries or people ease.

examples.en: Are you sick? You look pale.
After being sick for days, my face became pale.
She came out of the hospital with a pale face.
You stayed up all night, so your complexion looks pale.
The startled child's face went pale.
He was so pale that he looked almost ashen.

explain: 몸이 안 좋거나 놀라서 얼굴에 핏기가 없을 때 써요. 거의 얼굴이나 안색에만 쓰고, '핼쑥하다'와 비슷하게 쓰여요. 일상 대화에서는 '창백하다'나 '안색이 안 좋다'가 더 흔해요.
explain_en: It describes a face drained of color from illness or shock, and is almost only used for the face or complexion. It is used much like '핼쑥하다'. In daily talk '창백하다' or '안색이 안 좋다' is more common.

examples.ko: 보험을 해약하면 손해를 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you cancel the insurance, you might lose money.
I canceled my internet contract because of the move.

examples.ko: 해약하려면 한 달 전에 알려야 해요.
examples.en: To cancel, you have to give notice a month ahead.
I couldn't cancel because I didn't want to pay the penalty.
I called to ask them to cancel my gym membership.

examples.ko: 적금을 해약하고 그 돈으로 여행을 갔어요.
examples.en: I canceled my savings account and traveled with the money.

explain: 보험, 적금, 임대 같은 계약을 중간에 끝낼 때 써요. 휴대폰이나 카드는 '해지하다'라고 많이 말해요. 아직 시작하지 않은 예약은 '취소하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is used for ending a contract such as insurance, savings or a lease partway through. For phones and cards people often say '해지하다'. For a booking that hasn't started yet, '취소하다' is more natural.

examples.en: Wakame and laver are typical seaweeds.
I heard seaweed has a lot of dietary fiber.
I made soup with seaweed in it.
Seaweed was drying on the shore.

examples.ko: 건강을 생각해서 해조류 반찬을 자주 먹어요.
examples.en: For my health, I often eat seaweed side dishes.
At the mart, I first looked around the seaweed section.

explain: 미역, 다시마, 김처럼 바다에서 나는 풀 종류를 묶어 부르는 말이에요. 식사 때는 '미역', '김'처럼 하나씩 말하고, '해조류'는 식품 설명이나 과학 수업에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is a group name for sea plants like wakame, kelp and laver. At meals people name each one, such as '미역' or '김', while '해조류' mostly appears in food descriptions and science classes.

examples.en: Nobody will do you any harm.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 나중에 해코지할까 봐 무서워요.
examples.en: I'm afraid that person might try to harm me later.

examples.ko: 누가 제 자전거에 해코지를 했나 봐요.
examples.en: Someone seems to have tampered with my bike out of spite.
I couldn't speak up because I feared retaliation.

examples.ko: 그 개는 사람에게 해코지는 안 하니까 걱정 마세요.
examples.en: That dog doesn't hurt people, so don't worry.

examples.ko: 해코지 같은 짓은 절대 하지 마세요.
examples.en: Never do anything spiteful like that.

explain: 남에게 몰래 또는 일부러 해를 끼치는 짓을 말해요. 대개 '해코지하다', '해코지를 당하다'처럼 쓰고, 말로 할 때 자주 나오는 구어적인 말이에요. 앙갚음하려는 나쁜 마음이 느껴져요.
explain_en: It means deliberately or secretly causing someone harm. It is usually used as '해코지하다' or '해코지를 당하다' and is a fairly colloquial word. It carries a sense of malicious intent, like payback.

examples.en: A sea breeze is blowing, so the beach is cool.
I bought garlic grown in the sea breeze.
The sea breeze blows from the sea to the land during the day.
My hair feels sticky because of the sea breeze.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 해풍에 강한 나무를 심어요.
examples.en: This village plants trees that stand up to the sea wind.
Fish dried in the sea breeze tastes good.

explain: 바다에서 불어오는 바람이에요. 반대로 육지에서 바다 쪽으로 부는 바람은 '육풍'이라고 해요. 농수산물을 소개할 때 '해풍 맞은 ~'라는 표현을 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: This is wind blowing in from the sea. The opposite, wind blowing from land to sea, is '육풍'. In product descriptions of farm and sea foods you often see phrases like '해풍 맞은 ~' (sea-breeze-grown).

examples.en: This novel overflows with humor.

examples.ko: 탈춤에는 해학과 풍자가 함께 들어 있어요.
examples.en: Mask dance contains both humor and satire.

examples.ko: 옛이야기 속 해학을 지금도 즐길 수 있어요.
examples.en: We can still enjoy the humor in old tales.
That cartoonist is famous for humorous drawings.
The author's wit made me laugh naturally.
The humor in traditional Korean stories is warm.

explain: 웃음 속에 따뜻함이 담긴 익살을 말해요. 날카롭게 비꼬는 '풍자'와 짝으로 자주 나와서, 문학 수업에서 '해학과 풍자'라고 함께 배워요. 일상에서 웃긴 말은 '유머'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means jest with warmth in the laughter. It often pairs with '풍자' (satire, which bites sharply), so in literature class you learn '해학과 풍자' together. In everyday talk, funny things are just called '유머'.

examples.en: That movie depicted a reunion with a first love.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 해후 장면에서 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: I cried at the scene where the two met again.

examples.ko: 오랜 이별 끝에 가족의 해후가 이루어졌어요.
examples.en: After a long separation, the family was reunited.

examples.ko: 뜻밖의 해후에 서로 말을 잇지 못했어요.
examples.en: At the unexpected reunion, they couldn't find words.
The joy of reunion was brief and then came another parting.
The reunion was short but stayed in my memory for a long time.

explain: 오랫동안 헤어졌다가 다시 만나는 것을 말하는데, 뜻밖의 만남이라는 느낌이 있어요. 글이나 영화 소개 같은 곳에서 주로 쓰고, 일상에서는 '다시 만나다'나 '재회'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It means meeting again after a long separation, often with a feel of an unexpected encounter. It is mostly used in writing and movie descriptions, while daily speech prefers '다시 만나다' or '재회'.

examples.en: After being sick, your face has become quite gaunt.

examples.ko: 요즘 잠을 못 잤는지 핼쑥해 보여요.
examples.en: You look haggard, maybe because you haven't slept lately.
I'm worried about my coworker who came to work looking gaunt.

examples.ko: 그는 병이 나은 뒤에도 얼굴이 핼쑥했어요.
examples.en: His face was still gaunt even after he recovered.
He looked thin and gaunt from studying for the exam.
You worried that I look haggard, but I'm fine.

explain: 몸이 안 좋거나 지쳐서 얼굴에 핏기가 없고 야윈 듯 보일 때 써요. '핼쑥해지다', '핼쑥해 보이다'처럼 자주 쓰고 '해쓱하다'와 거의 같게 쓰여요. 외모에 대한 말이라 상대에게 직접 말할 때는 조심하는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: It describes a face that looks drained of color and thin from illness or exhaustion. It is often used as '핼쑥해지다' or '핼쑥해 보이다' and is used almost like '해쓱하다'. Because it comments on looks, be careful when saying it directly to someone.
